item.title: A small question: Re: A small question
item.content:encoded:
Does anyone know why this is said,

Because readers don't find the material interesting? If something doesn't interest them on the mainsite, they're not obligated to explain exactly why the piece didn't spark their interest. If someone is expecting thorough critique from a reviewer, the forums and IRC chatrooms are the place to look.

because I am curious as to whether this helpful to the author

While it's not the most helpful feedback, it's more helpful than nothing at all. Disliking something for not being interesting enough is different from disliking something for being too long-winded and a slog to read, or disliking something because it uses a color scheme or unique format that is disorienting or difficult to follow.

as one person could find it disinterestong but the next could find it absolutely fascinating.

Just because some people find something interesting does not mean everyone else has to feel the same way, and vice versa. People can disagree with others about the kind of article they like to read. Sometimes an author has to just shrug and accept a downvote. Just because someone else likes something does not make it wrong to dislike the same thing for personal preference reasons.

item.title: How many times should I ask for a critique?: Re: How many times should I ask for a critique?
item.content:encoded:
If they leave a placeholder and a time (Such as "Will crit within 24 hours") you can PM them after the time is up to remind them. If they don't respond, don't spam them with requests. If they've critiqued your idea and you've edited it, you can PM them again to see if they'll take another look. If someone tells you no or that they're busy, stop asking them since they're probably busy or just don't want to review it. Honestly, if you act respectfully towards the people doing you a favor, they'll have no issue critiquing you further, assuming time/life/whatever allows.

I suggest PMing more people (that you think, based on the butt squad roster, will be a good fit for critting) and stopping by our Crit Chat (#thecritters, the guide I linked there will teach you everything.) There are a lot more reviewers than just the ones on the butterfly squad roster that will help out there.

I hope this helped!

item.title: How many times should I ask for a critique?: How many times should I ask for a critique?
item.content:encoded:
How many times is it socially acceptable to ask a reviewer to critique your idea via Wikidot PM? I'm new to writing and I've gotten a couple of critiques from people in the Butterfly Squad on my idea.

I understand that most reviewers are busy reviewing and have real life commitments. Would it be annoying for me to ask them to review my idea again after I revised it multiple times? Two reviewers have looked at my idea and have both made two critiques, would it be fine if I asked them to look over it again? I feel like I would be annoying them if I asked them again, but I feel like getting the same reviewer to look over it would be beneficial because they can add on to previous critiques.

If I shouldn't message one reviewer multiple times, should I get a greater number of reviewers to look over the idea? If so, how many?

This is probably a stupid question but I don't want to overstep/seem annoying.

item.title: How would the Foundation deal with a suicidal witness: Re: How would the Foundation deal with a suicidal witness
item.content:encoded: Thanks!

item.title: How would the Foundation deal with a suicidal witness: Re: How would the Foundation deal with a suicidal witness
item.content:encoded:
I think your answer is a good one and one worth writing. Something similar happened in SCP-2420, so it's not the "wrong" answer.

Personal stories like that are more interesting to me as a reader than "asshole Foundation does bad shit." My main advice would be to make sure to treat him like a real person, not just a stereotype or "cartoon character." You might want to do a bit of reading about mental illness, too.

item.title: How would the Foundation deal with a suicidal witness: How would the Foundation deal with a suicidal witness
item.content:encoded:
Hey,

I'm writing an SCP, in which there's an old man (70) piloting an anomalous car. He was forced to quit his job as a stuntman, has a boring life, barely enough money, and on top of that, his only remaining friend died, leaving him the sports car in the will. He snaps, loads up on drugs and booms it to California.

Now, the Foundation reels him in together with the car and puts him in a padded cell. During his interviews, these issues come to light and the Ethics Committee interjects in the Foundation's plan to just amnesticise him and let him go, as the man is a walking catastrophe and is dangerous to both himself and others.

How would the Foundation approach such a problem? My idea is that they decide to keep him busy with the guys down at the Site's mechanic shop and send a disguised psychiatrist down, but it's a shot in the dark.

item.title: Promoting New Tale: Re: Promoting New Tale
item.content:encoded: I doubt it was only read 5 times, some people will read and novote, some will downvote and some will upvote. However, you've pretty much done all you can since you've posted to the announcements forum and plugged in 19. Quite honestly, with series its harder to get views and votes. Just be patient and keep plugging, just be sure not to be annoying with it and follow chat rules.

item.title: Site Dossier Help: Re: Site Dossier Help
item.content:encoded: As a general note, it's considered common courtesy to let authors know if you're going to reference their work in a piece you're writing. Both to make sure they're not unpleasantly caught off-guard if they see the crosslink, and to potentially get suggestions on how to correctly portray their content.

item.title: Site Dossier Help: Re: Site Dossier Help
item.content:encoded: You're able to, yes. Authors tend to use site dossiers as little hubs for their articles that take place in the same setting (a surprisingly common gimmick) but if the vibe you're going for is helped by the inclusion of other articles then go for it.
